title: Geometry - Lesson 5 Assessment: Construct and Verify Parallel Lines
description: Show mastery by choosing construction steps, checking accuracy, and explaining why a constructed line is parallel.

questions.question: Which statement describes parallel lines?
options: Lines that cross at one point
Lines in the same plane that do not intersect
Lines that always form right angles
questions.explanation: Parallel lines are coplanar lines that do not intersect.

questions.question: Which reason best justifies a copied-angle parallel construction?
options: Equal corresponding angles imply the lines are parallel
All acute angles create parallel lines
A longer line is more likely to be parallel
questions.explanation: The copied-angle method works because equal corresponding angles are a test for parallel lines.

questions.question: A corresponding angle on the original line measures $117^\circ$. What angle should be copied at point $P$?
questions.explanation: The corresponding angle must be copied with the same measure, $117^\circ$.

questions.question: A line drawn through $P$ is automatically parallel to $\ell$ because it passes through the required point.
questions.explanation: Passing through P is only one condition. The new line must also have the same direction as the given line.

questions.question: The shortest distance between two parallel lines is measured along a line that is ______ to both lines.
questions.explanation: Distance between parallel lines is measured perpendicularly.

questions.question: Which sequence is best for the protractor method?
options: Draw a random line through P, then label it parallel
Measure the angle at the given line, copy the corresponding angle at P, then draw through P
Measure the length of the given line, then draw a line with the same length
Draw two perpendicular lines and erase one
questions.explanation: The protractor method relies on copying the same corresponding angle at P.

questions.question: If two perpendicular distances between two drawn lines are equal, that supports the conclusion that the lines are parallel.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines remain the same perpendicular distance apart.

questions.question: A student uses a set square and ruler but rotates the set square before drawing through $P$. Explain the error.
questions.correctAnswer: Rotating the set square changes the direction of the edge, so the new line may not be parallel. The set square should slide without rotating.
questions.explanation: The set-square method works only when the tool keeps the same orientation while sliding.

questions.question: Write a complete conclusion if line $m$ was constructed through $P$ parallel to line $\ell$.
questions.correctAnswer: Line m passes through P and m is parallel to ell, written $m \parallel \ell$.
questions.explanation: A complete conclusion names the point condition and the parallel relationship.

questions.question: You copied a $74^\circ$ corresponding angle at point $P$ and drew line $m$. Explain why $m \parallel \ell$.
questions.correctAnswer: The corresponding angles are both 74 degrees, so they are congruent. Equal corresponding angles imply the two lines are parallel, so $m \parallel \ell$.
questions.explanation: The reasoning must connect the equal angle measures to the parallel-line relationship.
